limitations: This create-only request is an explicit closure over the discovery assignment; an empty reviewer_added_requests array means no reviewer-added candidates were found.
Ranking evidence and candidate material fingerprints are copied exactly from the bound discovery capsule and do not replace final source review.

reviewer_added_requests.discovery_reason: The target defines measurable product acceptance and already maps criteria to validation signals, while quality-test-gate consumes observable acceptance to select and judge proof. The lightweight contracts cannot establish the non-duplicating handoff or which skill owns the acceptance-to-signal map, so full candidate material is required.

Engineering-change-analysis owns broad source-backed preparation and impact proof, while architecture-impact-reviewer owns placement and structural verdicts for module-boundary risk. Their lightweight contracts leave the selection and delegation boundary under-specified, so full candidate material is needed to test overlap and routing.

The target owns observable exclusions and version limits and explicitly treats compatibility pressure as a reason to reopen scope, while version-compatibility owns consumer inventory, mixed-version behavior, migration, and retirement evidence. Full material is required to verify that version constraints are routed rather than silently accepted as non-goals.

Repository-impact-inspection returns owner, placement, consumer, and residual-risk evidence, while architecture-impact-reviewer returns a placement decision, architecture verdict, and structural risk. Because both are triggered by cross-module impact and share placement outputs, full candidate material is needed to prove the evidence-gathering versus decision boundary.

Requirement-structuring already covers actors, outcomes, dependencies, owners, and acceptance trace, while use-case-modeling specializes actor authority, paths, state effects, termination guarantees, and the same acceptance trace. The boundary catalog is insufficient to determine when structured requirements must hand off to a use-case model, so full material is required.

Scenario-decomposition includes abuse paths at changed trust boundaries and routes deeper attacker analysis to a security owner, while threat-modeling owns reachability, protected outcomes, control placement, bypass analysis, and residual risk. Full material is required to verify the handoff and prevent a generic abuse scenario from being treated as a completed threat model.
